=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:479-481 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The octopus-merge query lists merges touching protected paths without checking whether the merge itself differs from every parent, so clean merges combining already-authorized parent changes can be blocked.
  WHY: A clean octopus merge can have no associated merged PR, causing a legitimate release to be blocked; severity differed between reviewers (BLOCKER and MAJOR).
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:150-169 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The script force-pushes the stable tag without atomically verifying that the remote tag has not advanced since its release check.
  WHY: A concurrent release can advance the remote tag after this script's check, after which this script overwrites it with the older checked commit.
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:150-161 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The second `git fetch origin stable` may leave `refs/remotes/origin/stable` unchanged when both a branch and tag named `stable` exist, so the release check can use a stale branch reference.
  WHY: The check can pass against the stale reference even after the remote stable branch has advanced.
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:155-161 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: If the verification exits with status 7, the locally created annotated version tag remains and prevents a subsequent attempt from creating that tag.
  WHY: A retry fails because `git tag -a` refuses to overwrite the lingering local tag.
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:471 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: On Git versions that do not support `--remerge-diff`, the release check fails with an opaque error rather than identifying the required Git version.
  WHY: Operators running an older Git version receive no actionable indication that upgrading Git resolves the failure.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  expected_change_site: scripts/protected_path_authorization.py, `protected_merge_commits()`
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:479 uses bare `git rev-list --min-parents=3` without per-parent comparison; tests/test_protected_path_authorization.py:612 only verifies the positive case; tests/test_protected_path_authorization.py:617-627 only verifies the positive case; no negative-case test or per-parent comparison exists in the function body

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:479-480 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The octopus-merge query lists every octopus merge touching a protected path, without implementing the documented per-parent comparison.
  WHY: A clean octopus merge with no PR of its own can be blocked as an unauthorized protected edit and stop a legitimate release.
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:158-168 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The script does not re-verify the remote stable tag between its release check and force-push.
  WHY: A concurrent run can advance the remote stable tag, after which this invocation silently rolls it back.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: From AD-16 (docs/implement-plan/issue-4919-gate-protected-path-merges.md) and the plan (docs/plans/issue-4919-gate-protected-path-merges-plan.md line 183): "octopus merges that differ from every parent."
  Expected change site: scripts/protected_path_authorization.py, protected_merge_commits() function, at or after line 479
  Evidence of absence: Line 479 uses bare `git rev-list --min-parents=3 <range> -- <pathspecs>` which lists every octopus merge touching a protected path, not only those that differ from every parent. No per-parent diff-tree or equivalent comparison exists anywhere in the function body. The test at tests/test_protected_path_authorization.py:612 only verifies the positive case (an octopus merge with its own protected edit IS blocked), not the negative case (a clean octopus merge without its own edit is NOT blocked). The latter is the specific behavior AD-16 A selected.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:150-161 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `git fetch origin stable` may not update `refs/remotes/origin/stable` when both a branch and tag named `stable` exist on origin.
  WHY: The subsequent comparison can use the stale tracking branch and pass even if the remote stable branch has advanced.
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:479-480 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The octopus-merge query does not check whether a merge differs from every parent on a protected path.
  WHY: A clean octopus merge combining protected changes from different parents can be treated as an unauthorized edit and block the release.
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:168-169 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The moving stable tag is force-pushed without lease verification against the remote tag observed during the check.
  WHY: A concurrent release can advance the remote tag, and this force-push can roll it back.
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:155-161 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The local annotated tag is created before verifying whether origin/stable moved, leaving a lingering local tag when exit 7 is triggered.
  WHY: A subsequent attempt fails because `git tag -a` refuses to overwrite the existing local tag.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: From AD-16 / docstring / plan: "add two-parent merges whose git log --remerge-diff touches a protected path, plus octopus merges that differ from every parent."
  Expected change site: scripts/protected_path_authorization.py, protected_merge_commits() lines 479-481
  Evidence of absence: Line 479 executes bare git rev-list --min-parents=3 rev_range -- *PROTECTED_PATHSPECS, which lacks per-parent diff inspection (such as git diff-tree -c --name-only <sha> -- <pathspecs>) to verify that the octopus merge introduced protected-path modifications absent from all parents. In addition, tests/test_protected_path_authorization.py only tests an octopus merge that modified a protected path itself and omits testing that a clean octopus merge combining protected changes is not blocked.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:479 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The octopus-merge query lists every octopus merge touching a protected path without checking the documented per-parent condition.
  WHY: A clean octopus merge combining already-checked protected changes can lack an associated PR and block a legitimate release.
- scripts/mark-stable.sh:158-169 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The release verification does not guard the interval between its check and the force-push of the stable tag.
  WHY: A concurrent release can advance the remote tag before this script force-pushes its older checked commit.
- scripts/protected_path_authorization.py:471 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: An older Git version that does not recognize `--remerge-diff` causes a fail-closed error without an actionable explanation of the required version.
  WHY: Operators receive an opaque error rather than an indication that Git must be upgraded.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: AD-16 (docs/implement-plan/issue-4919-gate-protected-path-merges.md:46-47, mirrored in `docs/plans/issue-4919-gate-protected-path-merges-plan.md:182` and `agents.md:1211`): "add two-parent merges whose `git log --remerge-diff` touches a protected path, plus octopus merges that differ from every parent." The "differs from every parent" qualifier for octopus merges.
  Expected change site: scripts/protected_path_authorization.py, protected_merge_commits() function, the second query at line 479 (`_git(["rev-list", "--min-parents=3", rev_range, "--", *PROTECTED_PATHSPECS], git_dir)`).
  Evidence of absence: The current code passes the bare range + pathspecs to `git rev-list --min-parents=3`, which lists every octopus merge touching a protected path regardless of whether the merge commit's tree differs from each parent. No per-parent diff comparison (`git diff-tree`, `--combined-diff`, or equivalent) exists anywhere in `protected_merge_commits`. The added positive-case test `test_check_release_checks_an_octopus_merge_that_differs_from_every_parent` only proves that an octopus merge WITH its own edit gets blocked; the negative case (clean octopus merge) is uncovered, which is why this defect is invisible to CI. The docstring (lines 466-468), the plan text (line 182), AD-16, and `agents.md` (release section bullet) all describe the per-parent comparison that is absent.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
